title: Sharp bounds for stochastic proximal and projection estimators via radial dominance
summary: We study stochastic barycentric estimators for proximal points and metric projections obtained by exponentially reweighting Gaussian perturbations. Our main result is an abstract comparison theorem for probability measures with densities proportional to an exponential weight, under a radial dominance condition relative to a prescribed profile. This yields an explicit upper bound for the norm of the associated barycenter in terms of a one-dimensional comparison measure.
